clue.text: Somehow it's crime to imprison holy philosopher

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut something inside, so one piece goes within the other
somehow suggests the letters of the words it's crime are put together in some other way

parts.note: PI is crossword shorthand for pious, holy

explanation.surface: A thinker accused of locking up a saint, as if crime and philosophy had met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges ITSCRIME into EMRICIST, and 'to imprison' puts PI inside it after EM.
explanation.definitionFit: An empiricist is a thinker who holds that knowledge comes from experience, a school of philosophy.

clue.text: After revolution cease holding power and flee

indicators.note: holding means containing one piece within the other
after a revolution the letters of the word cease are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Rebels stop clinging to power and run away once the uprising is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After revolution' rearranges CEASE to ESCAE, and 'holding' puts P inside it before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to get away, to run from danger.

clue.text: Favourite holding love lines in verse

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains another

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on lines

explanation.surface: A favourite love poem with lines written in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O inside PET; RY for railway is a crossword convention for lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse and poetry are synonyms: writing in metre.

clue.text: Lame, injured, too out of sorts for play

indicators.note: out of sorts suggests the letters of the three words are jumbled and not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A player too hurt and miserable to go on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sorts' rearranges the fourteen letters of LAME, INJURED and TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of two star-crossed lovers from feuding Veronese families.

clue.text: It's the end of the night's viewing? Finish depressed

definitions.text: It's the end of the night's viewing?

parts.note: to finish is to close
depressed means down, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A gloomy viewer as the television day finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Older British TV channels stopped broadcasting overnight; the end of transmission was called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters used the term for the nightly end of transmission, when a channel stopped for the night.

clue.text: Chair for carrying little boy into school hospital

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a san, short for sanatorium, is the sick room at a British boarding school
Ed is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: A small boy being taken into the school sick bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts ED inside SAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan was an enclosed seat borne on poles by two porters, a carried chair.

clue.text: Party man among least agile

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the run of the words least agile

explanation.surface: A clumsy guest is singled out as the least nimble person at the do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the hidden word, found across leaST AGile.
explanation.definitionFit: The groom-to-be is the central figure of the bachelor celebration named after him, a stag do.

clue.text: A bottle damaged soft surface of piece of furniture

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of a bottle are broken and reassembled

parts.note: P is the music notation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A broken bottle has marked the soft finish on a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges ABOTTLE into TABLETO, with P after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper flat side of a dining or writing table is its working surface.

clue.text: Become discourteous when receiving king or queen

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the king goes inside the other piece

parts.note: to become discourteous is to get rude
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone turns rude on being granted an audience with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when receiving' puts R inside GET RUDE; 'or' is a link. The queen is the one in Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's mother is the queen of Denmark in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: A wife endures — he's off with a farewell!

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered or gone wrong

parts.note: only he is fodder; the 's stands for 'is', a link giving no letters

explanation.surface: A long-suffering wife puts up with it as her husband leaves with a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges AWIFEENDURESHE; the 's of he's is the verb 'is' joining fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The German phrase for goodbye, literally until we see again.

clue.text: The best stuff to cover wrinkles?

explanation.surface: An advert for top-quality face lotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The choicest part of a group is its finest layer, as skimmed from milk; it is also a lotion rubbed on ageing skin.

clue.text: This is the sixth!

parts.note: the clue points at its own number: count one, three, five and so on, and this clue's number is sixth in that sequence

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly counting a sixth attempt or a sixth item.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to its own grid number, 11, which is the sixth in the series 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven cannot be split into two equal whole numbers, so it belongs to the series of integers not divisible by two.

clue.text: Aim to get prize money having crossed river

indicators.note: the prize money is said to have gone across the river, so the river sits within it

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money awarded as a prize, as in boxing
the Po is a river in northern Italy

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to win a cash prize after fording a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having crossed' puts PO inside PURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim and an intention are synonyms: the goal one is working toward.

clue.text: We yearn to change — time for resolution?

indicators.note: to change these words is to alter the order of their letters

explanation.surface: People longing to reform themselves, looking for a moment to make a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges WEYEARN; 'resolution' looks like solving a problem but means a pledge made on 1 January.
explanation.definitionFit: The start of January is traditionally when people make pledges to improve themselves.

clue.text: Where progress is impossible and a U-turn must be made?

definitions.text: Where progress is impossible and a U-turn must be made?

parts.words: Where progress is impossible and a U-turn must be made?
parts.note: read literally, a dead end where a driver must turn round; figuratively, the point at which a venture can go no further

explanation.surface: A driver reaches a dead end and has to turn back.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the final point beyond which something cannot continue, pictured as a street running out.

clue.text: Given a good screw?

parts.note: reads as a vulgar innuendo, but means turned with a screwdriver until firm

explanation.surface: A cheeky double entendre.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw given plenty of turns is made secure and firm.

clue.text: Warbler to bring news of death sentence?

explanation.surface: A songbird bearing grim tidings of execution.
explanation.walkthrough: British judges once put on a square black cloth over their wig before passing a death sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A European songbird with a dark crown is one sense; the judge's headwear before pronouncing hanging is the other.

clue.text: Bad habit maybe, missing a hundred in sum

indicators.note: missing says the hundred is left out of the longer word

parts.note: an addiction is an example of a bad habit, hence maybe
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A bad habit drops a hundred from a total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes C from ADDICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is a calculation in which figures are totted up together.

clue.text: A nine days' wonder on the throne of England?

definitions.text: A nine days' wonder on the throne of England?

parts.words: A nine days' wonder on the throne of England?
parts.note: a nine days' wonder is a short-lived sensation; here it is taken literally as a monarch who reigned only nine days in 1553

explanation.surface: A fleeting sensation who briefly sat on England's throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tudor claimant proclaimed queen in July 1553 was deposed after nine days and later executed.
explanation.definitionFit: The great-niece of Henry VIII held the English crown for just nine days before Mary I took it.

clue.text: Nasty old bishop greeting dean outside

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: hi is a greeting
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
D is an abbreviation for dean

explanation.surface: A grumpy elderly bishop greets a dean in the cloister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts O and RR inside HI followed by D.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrid and nasty are synonyms: unpleasant.

clue.text: Mean little devil residing in the heavens

indicators.note: residing in says one piece lives inside the other

parts.note: the sky is the heavens
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: A stingy imp living up in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'residing in' puts IMP inside SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean here is skimpy in the sense of scanty or stingy, giving too little.

clue.text: Little child unwell, boy with lowered temperature

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for child
unwell means ill
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A sick little boy whose fever has come down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a feverish child, but the pieces are simply CH, ILL and ED in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chilled has been made cold, its heat reduced.

clue.text: Rubbish left out in lane at front of house

indicators.note: out says the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: drivel is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Bin bags put out in the lane in front of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from DRIVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The private road leading up to a home is a driveway.

clue.text: Hairy bunch in union's taking knock

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union, and the possessive adds S
to sock is to punch or knock

explanation.surface: A union taking a beating over something shaggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is only a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a tuft or clump, of grass or hair, growing in a thick bunch.

clue.text: Reference point for a London theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre in the West End used as a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard by which things are judged is a benchmark; it is also the name of a playhouse on Piccadilly Circus in London.

clue.text: Damage outside eastern women's quarters

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to damage is to harm

explanation.surface: Vandalism around the women's rooms of an Eastern palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts HARM round E.
explanation.definitionFit: In a traditional Muslim household the seraglio was the separate section where the wives lived.

clue.text: Long wood

explanation.surface: A tall stretch of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it; a conifer's timber is also used for furniture.

clue.text: Date set for match

parts.note: reads like a fixture for a sporting contest, but the match is a marriage and the date is when it takes place

explanation.surface: A fixture scheduled for a sports game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests football or tennis; here it is a couple being matched in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The day appointed for a couple's marriage ceremony is the date fixed for their union.
